content: # Terminal Portfolio Update [MIR_OS]:
- TYPE: Code Cleanup & Mobile Optimizations
- TARGET: Terminal Portfolio
- STATUS: Deployed
# THE_OBJECTIVE
As the project quickly grew, the main files were excessively getting out of hand and finding errors were taking too long. The goal was then to
break up the code into many components and ensure D.R.Y. was being followed.
# THE_EXECUTION
* [CODE_ORGANIZATION]: Took a giant 800-line file and split it up. Now, the virtual file system, the text documents, and the actual terminal commands all live in their own neat, separate files.
* [SMARTER_NAVIGATION]: Built a custom helper function that mimics how a real computer navigates folders. Now, complex commands like `cd ../../logs` work flawlessly.

* [MOBILE_FIXES]: Redesigned the 'quickstart' guide into a compact, two-column dashboard so it doesn't take up the whole screen. Also fixed a bug where long text was stretching the screen horizontally on phones.
# THE_ROADBLOCK

The terminal's logic for reading commands (`cd`, `cat`, and autocomplete) was getting repetitive. Every command had its own slightly different way of figuring out which folder the user wanted to go to, which left room for bugs and made the code messy.
# THE_RESOLUTION

Instead of repeating myself, I extracted that logic into a single 'Path Resolver' tool. Now, all commands share the exact same reliable map to find files. I also set up a cleaner command processor so the main app doesn't have to think about *how* to run a command—it just displays the result.
# NEXT_STEPS
Still need to work on the auto suggestion when going through multiple directories and such but I'll save that headache for another day

title: Terminal Portfolio Updates
content: # Terminal Portfolio Update [MIR_OS]:
- TYPE: System Architecture & Feature Release
- TARGET: Terminal Portfolio (MIR_OS V0.0.5)
- COMPONENT: VFS, CI/CD, Text Editing
- STATUS: Deployed
# THE_OBJECTIVE

Today’s goal was to: transform the terminal from a static read-only interface into a fully interactive operating system, and build a "hands-off" CI/CD pipeline so I can publish blog posts directly from a separate GitHub repository without touching the core React code.
# THE_EXECUTION
* [GITHUB ACTIONS]: Allowed for seamless CI/CD from one repository update to another. This was used in both updating my leetcode progress and this blog.

* [VIM_EDITOR]: Integrated a functional Vim-like text editor. Users can now create, edit, and save files directly into the terminal's Session RAM using authentic Vim commands (`:i`, `[ESC]`, `:wq`, `:q`).
* [FILE_MANAGEMENT]: Implemented the `rm` command. Users can delete their own session files, but the system actively guards against the deletion of core portfolio metadata (Permission Denied).
* [SYSTEM_MANUAL]: Added a comprehensive `help` command, featuring a visually distinct UI and a Vim Quickstart guide for recruiters unfamiliar with Linux environments.
* [DYNAMIC_VFS]: Built an "LOG BLOG" that dynamically mounts external JSON data into the Virtual File System on boot, allowing commands like `cd` and `ls` to instantly recognize new directories.
# THE_ROADBLOCK
Automating the blog sync was a multi-layered debugging session across three environments (Local Windows, GitHub Actions, and Vercel).

Vercel's strict TypeScript compiler blocked deployments due to unused function parameters. Meanwhile, the Python build script crashed because Windows PowerShell injected hidden UTF-16 Byte Order Marks (BOM) into my `.md` files. Finally, dynamically created folders threw "No such directory" errors because the terminal's input parser was aggressively lowercasing the user's input, causing case-sensitive mismatches in the Virtual File System.
# THE_RESOLUTION
* Silenced Vercel's strict TS errors using the underscore prefix standard (`_args`).
* Rewrote the Python file reader to fallback seamlessly between `utf-8-sig` and `utf-16`, using Regex to handle varying filename formats.
* Refactored the VFS to automatically convert all generated folders to lowercase, creating a foolproof navigation experience.
* Upgraded the `ls` command to contextually switch to a vertical layout when viewing blog directories to handle long filenames cleanly.
# NEXT_STEPS
The systems seems to be stable now. Next I would like to maybe add a theme changer as the green might not be for everyone.
